To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the administration of antibiotics to children before age 2 years increases risk for childhood obesity and that antibiotics administered to mothers during pregnancy and to infants during their first 3 months of life increase risk for asthma in children by the time they reach age 6.

(1) antibiotic use in early childhood is associated with increased risk for childhood obesity, (2) this association was stronger for children who had received antibiotics before the age of 2 years, (3) the effect was strongest for children who received antibiotics for more than one course, and (4) the effect was stronger in boys than in girls.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of antibiotics in early childhood on the development of obesity in children.
the effects of the administration of antibiotics to young children, and their potential role in increasing the risk of obesity in later years.
the effects of antibiotic exposure in utero on the gut microbiome, and its relationship to childhood asthma and allergy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
antibiotic use in early childhood is associated with a small but significant increase in childhood obesity, and that this effect is likely mediated by alterations in gut microbiota.
antibiotics in the first 2 years of life are not associated with an increased risk of obesity in children.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
antibiotic use in early childhood increases the risk of obesity.
the risk of childhood obesity is increased by antibiotic use in children younger than two years old.
the administration of antibiotics to children before the age of two years is associated with an increased risk for childhood obesity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the administration of antibiotics in the first 2 years of life is associated with increased childhood body mass index (BMI) and obesity risk.
the risk for obesity increases with the number of antibiotics administered before age 2 years, and the risk increases with each subsequent antibiotic course.
